functions.signature: Vector2 GetSplinePointCatmullRom(Vector2 p1, Vector2 p2, Vector2 p3, Vector2 p4, float t);
functions.description: Evaluate a Catmull-Rom spline at parameter t in [0..1].
requirements: t should be in the range [0.0f..1.0f] for typical use.

functions.name: GetSplinePointBezierQuad
functions.signature: Vector2 GetSplinePointBezierQuad(Vector2 p1, Vector2 c2, Vector2 p3, float t);
functions.description: Evaluate a quadratic Bezier curve at parameter t in [0..1].
requirements: t should be in the range [0.0f..1.0f] for typical use.

functions.name: GetSplinePointBezierCubic
functions.signature: Vector2 GetSplinePointBezierCubic(Vector2 p1, Vector2 c2, Vector2 c3, Vector2 p4, float t);
functions.description: Evaluate a cubic Bezier curve at parameter t in [0..1].
requirements: t should be in the range [0.0f..1.0f] for typical use.

functions.name: GetCameraForward
functions.description: Compute and return the camera's normalized forward/view direction vector (target - position). Intended for querying the camera’s current facing direction.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera with position and target set.
camera->position and camera->target should not be identical to avoid a zero-length direction vector and undefined normalization behavior.
camera->up is not used here, but overall camera basis consistency is recommended.

functions.name: GetCameraUp
functions.description: Return the camera's normalized up vector. The up vector need not be perpendicular to the forward vector.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera with a meaningful up vector.
camera->up should not be the zero vector to avoid undefined normalization behavior.

functions.name: GetCameraRight
functions.description: Compute and return the camera's normalized right vector as cross(GetCameraForward(), GetCameraUp()). Useful for strafing and building an orthonormal basis.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
camera->position and camera->target should not be identical (forward must be non-zero).
camera->up should be non-zero and not colinear with the forward direction to avoid a zero cross-product and undefined normalization behavior.

functions.name: CameraMoveForward
functions.signature: RLAPI void CameraMoveForward(Camera *camera, float distance, bool moveInWorldPlane);
functions.description: Translate the camera forward/backward by distance along its forward vector. When moveInWorldPlane is true, the movement is projected onto the world plane defined by the up vector (preventing vertical motion).
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
distance is in world units; positive moves toward target, negative moves backward.

If moveInWorldPlane is true, the function projects movement onto a plane using the dominant axis of camera->up; for predictable behavior camera->up should represent the world up direction and be near a principal axis.
Camera basis should be valid (forward non-zero).

functions.name: CameraMoveUp
functions.description: Translate the camera up/down by distance along its up vector, moving both position and target together.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera with a meaningful up vector.
distance is in world units; positive moves along up, negative opposite.
camera->up should not be zero to avoid a no-op or undefined behavior.

functions.name: CameraMoveRight
functions.signature: RLAPI void CameraMoveRight(Camera *camera, float distance, bool moveInWorldPlane);
functions.description: Translate the camera right/left by distance along its right vector. When moveInWorldPlane is true, the movement is projected onto the world plane defined by the up vector.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
distance is in world units; positive moves right, negative moves left.
Right vector requires forward and up to be valid and non-colinear.
If moveInWorldPlane is true, camera->up should represent the world up direction and be near a principal axis for predictable projection behavior.

functions.name: CameraMoveToTarget
functions.description: Adjust the distance from the camera position to its target by delta, moving the position along the forward axis. Positive delta increases the distance (zooms out); negative delta decreases it (zooms in). The resulting distance is clamped to a minimum of 0.001 to avoid collapsing onto the target.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
camera->position and camera->target should not be identical to avoid zero-length forward when recomputing position.
delta is in world units; sign controls in/out movement.

functions.name: CameraYaw
functions.signature: RLAPI void CameraYaw(Camera *camera, float angle, bool rotateAroundTarget);
functions.description: Rotate the camera around its up axis (yaw: look left/right). If rotateAroundTarget is true, orbit around the target (move position); otherwise rotate the view direction around the camera position (move target). Angle is in radians.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
angle must be provided in radians (as explicitly documented).
camera->up must be a valid non-zero vector (rotation axis).
camera->position and camera->target should not be identical (view vector must be non-zero).

functions.name: CameraPitch
functions.signature: RLAPI void CameraPitch(Camera *camera, float angle, bool lockView, bool rotateAroundTarget, bool rotateUp);
functions.description: Rotate the camera around its right axis (pitch: look up/down). Angle is in radians. When lockView is true, the function clamps the pitch to prevent flipping over. If rotateAroundTarget is true, orbit around the target; otherwise rotate around the camera position. If rotateUp is true, also rotate the up vector around the right axis.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
angle must be provided in radians (as explicitly documented).
Requires a valid right axis, thus forward and up must be valid and not colinear.
When lockView is true, pitch is internally clamped to avoid over-rotation; callers should not rely on exact angle application in that case.
camera->position and camera->target should not be identical (view vector must be non-zero).

functions.name: CameraRoll
functions.description: Rotate the camera around its forward axis (roll: tilt head left/right). Angle is in radians. Only the up vector is rotated; position and target remain related via forward.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
angle must be provided in radians (as explicitly documented).
camera->position and camera->target should not be identical (forward axis must be non-zero).

functions.name: GetCameraViewMatrix
functions.description: Build and return the camera view (look-at) matrix from position, target, and up using MatrixLookAt.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
Look-at requires a non-zero forward (target != position) and an up vector that is not parallel to forward.

functions.name: GetCameraProjectionMatrix
functions.description: Build and return the camera projection matrix. For CAMERA_PERSPECTIVE, uses perspective with fovy (degrees), aspect, and fixed near/far planes. For CAMERA_ORTHOGRAPHIC, builds an orthographic matrix with extents derived from fovy/2 and aspect. If projection is neither value, returns identity.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera with projection set to CAMERA_PERSPECTIVE or CAMERA_ORTHOGRAPHIC; otherwise identity is returned.
aspect should be positive and non-zero for meaningful results.
For perspective: camera->fovy should be a sensible field-of-view in degrees (typically 0 < fovy < 180) to avoid invalid projections.
Near/far planes are fixed to CAMERA_CULL_DISTANCE_NEAR and CAMERA_CULL_DISTANCE_FAR.

functions.name: UpdateCamera
functions.description: Update the camera each frame based on user input and the specified mode (CAMERA_FREE, CAMERA_FIRST_PERSON, CAMERA_THIRD_PERSON, CAMERA_ORBITAL, or CAMERA_CUSTOM). Handles rotation, movement, panning, zooming, and gamepad input using raylib input APIs. Only compiled when RCAMERA_STANDALONE is not defined.
requirements: Available only when RCAMERA_STANDALONE is not defined (depends on raylib input functions).
camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera.
mode must be one of the defined CameraMode values; behavior varies by mode.
Should be called once per frame to apply input-driven updates; relies on GetFrameTime() for speed scaling.
Requires a functioning raylib input context (keyboard/mouse/gamepad).

functions.name: UpdateCameraPro
functions.signature: void UpdateCameraPro(Camera *camera, Vector3 movement, Vector3 rotation, float zoom);
functions.description: Update the camera using caller-provided movement and rotation deltas and a zoom value, without directly reading input. movement: x=forward/back, y=right/left, z=up/down (world units). rotation: x=yaw, y=pitch, z=roll in degrees. zoom adjusts distance to target (positive zooms out, negative zooms in). Applies clamped pitch, rotates around position (not target), and moves in world plane for forward/right.
requirements: camera must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized Camera with consistent basis (position != target, up non-zero, forward and up not colinear).
rotation components are in degrees and will be converted internally to radians.
movement components are in world units along the camera’s local axes; forward/right motion is constrained to the world plane.
zoom is in world units; positive increases distance to target, negative decreases it (minimum distance internally clamped to 0.001).

functions.name: rlMatrixMode
functions.description: Selects which internal matrix (modelview or projection) subsequent matrix operations modify. Acts like OpenGL’s glMatrixMode for rlgl’s state machine.
requirements: mode must be one of RL_MODELVIEW or RL_PROJECTION; RL_TEXTURE is not supported in GL33/ES2 path
If using GL33/ES2 backend, rlglInit() must have been called before use

functions.name: rlPushMatrix
functions.description: Pushes the current matrix onto the internal matrix stack. In modelview mode it switches to the transform stack for subsequent transforms until rlPopMatrix is called.
requirements: Matrix stack has a maximum size RL_MAX_MATRIX_STACK_SIZE (default 32); pushing beyond logs an error
Call after rlglInit() and after having selected a matrix mode with rlMatrixMode

functions.name: rlPopMatrix
functions.description: Pops the last matrix from the internal stack back into the current matrix. If the stack empties in modelview mode, it resets to the modelview and disables transformRequired.
requirements: There must be at least one matrix pushed; otherwise it is a no-op
Call after rlPushMatrix for proper stack usage

functions.name: rlLoadIdentity
functions.description: Replaces the current matrix with the identity matrix.
requirements: A current matrix must be selected via rlMatrixMode
rlglInit() must have been called in GL33/ES2 path

functions.name: rlTranslatef
functions.signature: void rlTranslatef(float x, float y, float z);
functions.description: Multiplies the current matrix by a translation matrix translating by (x,y,z).
requirements: A current matrix must be selected via rlMatrixMode
Angle units not involved; arguments are linear units
rlglInit() required for GL33/ES2 path

functions.name: rlRotatef
functions.signature: void rlRotatef(float angle, float x, float y, float z);
functions.description: Multiplies the current matrix by a rotation around axis (x,y,z) by angle degrees. Axis is normalized internally.
requirements: angle is in degrees
If axis length is zero, rotation degenerates (no-op)
A current matrix must be selected via rlMatrixMode

functions.name: rlScalef
functions.signature: void rlScalef(float x, float y, float z);
functions.description: Multiplies the current matrix by a scaling matrix scaling each axis by x, y, z.
requirements: A current matrix must be selected via rlMatrixMode

functions.name: rlMultMatrixf
functions.description: Multiplies the current matrix by another 4x4 matrix provided as a 16-float array (column-major, OpenGL style).
requirements: matf must point to at least 16 floats in column-major order

functions.name: rlFrustum
functions.signature: void rlFrustum(double left, double right, double bottom, double top, double znear, double zfar);
functions.description: Multiplies the current matrix by a perspective frustum matrix defined by the given clipping planes. Equivalent to glFrustum semantics.
requirements: right != left and top != bottom and zfar != znear to avoid division by zero
znear and zfar should be positive and znear > 0 for a valid frustum

functions.name: rlOrtho
functions.signature: void rlOrtho(double left, double right, double bottom, double top, double znear, double zfar);
functions.description: Multiplies the current matrix by an orthographic projection matrix defined by the given planes. Equivalent to glOrtho semantics.
requirements: right != left and top != bottom and zfar != znear to avoid division by zero

functions.name: rlViewport
functions.signature: void rlViewport(int x, int y, int width, int height);
functions.description: Sets the OpenGL viewport to the specified rectangle.
requirements: width and height must be non-negative
An active GL context is required

functions.name: rlSetClipPlanes
functions.description: Sets internal near and far clip plane distances used by rlgl for depth increment and culling related logic.
requirements: nearPlane and farPlane are stored as doubles; no specific constraints enforced

functions.name: rlGetCullDistanceNear
functions.description: Returns the current stored near culling plane distance.

functions.name: rlGetCullDistanceFar
functions.description: Returns the current stored far culling plane distance.

functions.name: rlBegin
functions.description: Begins immediate-mode style vertex submission for the specified primitive mode (RL_LINES, RL_TRIANGLES, RL_QUADS). Batches draw calls internally.
requirements: mode must be one of RL_LINES, RL_TRIANGLES, RL_QUADS
Must be paired with rlEnd
In GL33/ES2 path, an internal batch must be active (rlglInit creates one)

functions.name: rlEnd
functions.description: Ends the current immediate-mode submission begun with rlBegin. Advances internal depth slightly to separate draw layers.
requirements: Call only after a matching rlBegin

functions.name: rlVertex2i
functions.description: Submits a 2D vertex with integer coordinates. Z is taken from current batch depth.
requirements: Must be called between rlBegin/rlEnd
If batching limit would be exceeded, the system will flush mid-primitive only at valid boundaries

functions.name: rlVertex2f
functions.description: Submits a 2D vertex with float coordinates. Z is taken from current batch depth.
requirements: Must be called between rlBegin/rlEnd

functions.name: rlVertex3f
functions.signature: void rlVertex3f(float x, float y, float z);
functions.description: Submits a 3D vertex with float coordinates. Applies current transform if active. Also writes current texcoord, normal, and color to buffers.
requirements: Must be called between rlBegin/rlEnd
Batch limits apply; function may trigger a flush to avoid breaking primitives

functions.name: rlTexCoord2f
functions.description: Sets the current texture coordinates used by subsequent rlVertex* calls.
requirements: Call before rlVertex* to affect that vertex
Primarily used with RL_QUADS batching

functions.name: rlNormal3f
functions.signature: void rlNormal3f(float x, float y, float z);
functions.description: Sets the current normal vector (normalized internally). Applies current transform’s rotation to the normal if transformRequired.
requirements: Zero-length normal gets normalized to zero; avoid all-zero inputs for meaningful lighting
Affects subsequent rlVertex* submissions

functions.name: rlColor4ub
functions.signature: void rlColor4ub(unsigned char r, unsigned char g, unsigned char b, unsigned char a);
functions.description: Sets the current vertex color as 8-bit RGBA used by subsequent rlVertex* calls.
requirements: Values are 0-255 per channel

functions.name: rlColor3f
functions.signature: void rlColor3f(float x, float y, float z);
functions.description: Sets the current vertex color from normalized float RGB; alpha defaults to 255.
requirements: Inputs typically in 0.0-1.0; values are multiplied by 255 and clamped by conversion to unsigned char

functions.name: rlColor4f
functions.signature: void rlColor4f(float x, float y, float z, float w);
functions.description: Sets the current vertex color from normalized float RGBA.
requirements: Inputs typically in 0.0-1.0; values are multiplied by 255 and clamped by conversion to unsigned char

functions.name: rlEnableVertexArray
functions.description: Binds the given VAO if VAOs are supported, returning true on success.
requirements: vaoId must be a valid vertex array object name
Returns false if VAO is not supported or bind failed

functions.name: rlDisableVertexArray
functions.description: Unbinds any currently bound VAO (binds 0) if supported.

functions.name: rlEnableVertexBuffer
functions.description: Binds the given VBO to GL_ARRAY_BUFFER.
requirements: id must be a valid buffer object name

functions.name: rlDisableVertexBuffer
functions.description: Unbinds any buffer from GL_ARRAY_BUFFER (binds 0).

functions.name: rlEnableVertexBufferElement
functions.description: Binds the given element/index buffer to GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER.
requirements: id must be a valid buffer object name

functions.name: rlDisableVertexBufferElement
functions.description: Unbinds any buffer from GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER (binds 0).

functions.name: rlEnableVertexAttribute
functions.description: Enables a vertex attribute array at the given index.
requirements: index must correspond to an active attribute in the currently bound VAO/VBO setup

functions.name: rlDisableVertexAttribute
functions.description: Disables a vertex attribute array at the given index.
requirements: index must be a valid attribute index

functions.name: rlEnableStatePointer
functions.description: OpenGL 1.1 path: enables client state array and sets its pointer for legacy arrays (vertex, texcoord, normal, color). No effect on GL33/ES2 path.
requirements: vertexAttribType must be one of GL_VERTEX_ARRAY, GL_TEXTURE_COORD_ARRAY, GL_NORMAL_ARRAY, GL_COLOR_ARRAY
buffer must point to compatible data with correct component counts

functions.name: rlDisableStatePointer
functions.description: OpenGL 1.1 path: disables a client state array corresponding to vertexAttribType. No effect on GL33/ES2 path.
requirements: vertexAttribType must be a valid client state enum

functions.name: rlActiveTextureSlot
functions.description: Activates texture unit GL_TEXTURE0 + slot.
requirements: slot must be within the GPU’s supported texture unit range

functions.name: rlEnableTexture
functions.description: Binds a 2D texture id to GL_TEXTURE_2D. On GL11 also enables GL_TEXTURE_2D.
requirements: id must be a valid GL texture name

functions.name: rlDisableTexture
functions.description: Unbinds GL_TEXTURE_2D (binds 0). On GL11 also disables the target.

functions.name: rlEnableTextureCubemap
functions.description: Binds a cubemap texture id to GL_TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP.
requirements: Available and meaningful only on GL33/ES2
id must be a valid cubemap texture name

functions.name: rlDisableTextureCubemap
functions.description: Unbinds GL_TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP (binds 0).
requirements: Only effective on GL33/ES2

functions.name: rlTextureParameters
functions.signature: void rlTextureParameters(unsigned int id, int param, int value);
functions.description: Sets texture parameters for a 2D texture (wrap, filter, anisotropy, LOD bias). Binds texture, sets parameter, then unbinds.
requirements: id must be a valid 2D texture
param must be one of RL_TEXTURE_WRAP_S, RL_TEXTURE_WRAP_T, RL_TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER, RL_TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER, RL_TEXTURE_FILTER_ANISOTROPIC, RL_TEXTURE_MIPMAP_BIAS_RATIO
For RL_TEXTURE_FILTER_ANISOTROPIC, extension support required; value must not exceed reported maxAnisotropyLevel

functions.name: rlCubemapParameters
functions.signature: void rlCubemapParameters(unsigned int id, int param, int value);
functions.description: Sets texture parameters for a cubemap (wrap, filter, anisotropy, LOD bias).
requirements: Only on GL33/ES2
id must be a valid cubemap texture
param and value restrictions as per rlTextureParameters; mirror clamp requires extension support

functions.name: rlEnableShader
functions.description: Uses/binds the given shader program (glUseProgram).
requirements: id must be a linked GL program object

functions.name: rlDisableShader
functions.description: Unbinds any current shader program (glUseProgram(0)).

functions.name: rlEnableFramebuffer
functions.description: Binds the given framebuffer object to GL_FRAMEBUFFER for rendering.
requirements: id must be a valid FBO name

functions.name: rlDisableFramebuffer
functions.description: Binds the default framebuffer (id 0).

functions.name: rlGetActiveFramebuffer
functions.description: Returns the currently bound draw framebuffer (GL_DRAW_FRAMEBUFFER_BINDING where available).
requirements: Requires GL33/ES3 to query draw binding; returns 0 otherwise

functions.name: rlActiveDrawBuffers
functions.description: Activates multiple draw color attachments for the current framebuffer using glDrawBuffers. Up to 8 supported by this API.
requirements: Only available on GL33/ES3
count must be >= 1 and <= 8 for this call; more will be clamped/logged

functions.name: rlBlitFramebuffer
functions.signature: void rlBlitFramebuffer(int srcX, int srcY, int srcWidth, int srcHeight, int dstX, int dstY, int dstWidth, int dstHeight, int bufferMask);
functions.description: Blits the currently bound read/draw framebuffers rectangle from src to dst with nearest filtering.
requirements: Only available on GL33/ES3
Appropriate FBOs must be bound to read/draw targets and compatible with bufferMask (e.g., GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT)

functions.name: rlBindFramebuffer
functions.signature: void rlBindFramebuffer(unsigned int target, unsigned int framebuffer);
functions.description: Binds a framebuffer to the specified target (e.g., GL_FRAMEBUFFER). Thin wrapper around glBindFramebuffer.
requirements: target must be a valid FBO target enum
framebuffer must be a valid FBO name or 0

functions.name: rlEnableColorBlend
functions.description: Enables GL blending (glEnable(GL_BLEND)).

functions.name: rlDisableColorBlend
functions.description: Disables GL blending (glDisable(GL_BLEND)).

functions.name: rlEnableDepthTest
functions.description: Enables GL depth testing (glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST)).

functions.name: rlDisableDepthTest
functions.description: Disables GL depth testing (glDisable(GL_DEPTH_TEST)).

functions.name: rlEnableDepthMask
functions.description: Enables depth writes (glDepthMask(GL_TRUE)).

functions.name: rlDisableDepthMask
functions.description: Disables depth writes (glDepthMask(GL_FALSE)).

functions.name: rlEnableBackfaceCulling
functions.description: Enables face culling (glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE)).

functions.name: rlDisableBackfaceCulling
functions.description: Disables face culling (glDisable(GL_CULL_FACE)).

functions.name: rlColorMask
functions.signature: void rlColorMask(bool r, bool g, bool b, bool a);
functions.description: Sets the color write mask for the framebuffer (glColorMask).

functions.name: rlSetCullFace
functions.description: Sets which face to cull using glCullFace. Supports RL_CULL_FACE_BACK and RL_CULL_FACE_FRONT.
requirements: mode must be RL_CULL_FACE_BACK or RL_CULL_FACE_FRONT

functions.name: rlEnableScissorTest
functions.description: Enables scissor testing (glEnable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST)).

functions.name: rlDisableScissorTest
functions.description: Disables scissor testing (glDisable(GL_SCISSOR_TEST)).

functions.name: rlScissor
functions.signature: void rlScissor(int x, int y, int width, int height);
functions.description: Sets the scissor rectangle (glScissor).
requirements: width and height must be non-negative

functions.name: rlEnablePointMode
functions.description: Enables polygon rasterization to POINT mode and GL_PROGRAM_POINT_SIZE on GL11/GL33.
requirements: Only effective on GL11/GL33; not supported on OpenGL ES 2.0

functions.name: rlDisablePointMode
functions.description: Restores polygon mode to FILL from POINT on GL11/GL33.
requirements: Only effective on GL11/GL33

functions.name: rlSetPointSize
functions.description: Sets GL point size (glPointSize) for GL 1.1 path.
requirements: Only effective on GL11

functions.name: rlGetPointSize
functions.description: Gets current GL point size (GL_POINT_SIZE) on GL11; returns 1 on other backends.

functions.name: rlEnableWireMode
functions.description: Sets polygon rasterization to wireframe (GL_LINE) on GL11/GL33.
requirements: Only effective on GL11/GL33

functions.name: rlDisableWireMode
functions.description: Sets polygon rasterization back to fill (GL_FILL) on GL11/GL33.
requirements: Only effective on GL11/GL33

functions.name: rlSetLineWidth
functions.description: Sets GL line width (glLineWidth).

functions.name: rlGetLineWidth
functions.description: Queries current GL line width via glGetFloatv(GL_LINE_WIDTH).

functions.name: rlEnableSmoothLines
functions.description: Enables line smoothing (GL_LINE_SMOOTH) on GL11/GL33.
requirements: Only effective on GL11/GL33

functions.name: rlDisableSmoothLines
functions.description: Disables line smoothing on GL11/GL33.
requirements: Only effective on GL11/GL33

functions.name: rlEnableStereoRender
functions.description: Enables rlgl’s stereo rendering mode; internal state will render each batch per-eye with separate matrices.
requirements: Only tracked/used on GL33/ES2

functions.name: rlDisableStereoRender
functions.description: Disables rlgl’s stereo rendering mode.
requirements: Only tracked/used on GL33/ES2

functions.name: rlIsStereoRenderEnabled
functions.description: Returns whether stereo rendering is enabled.

functions.name: rlClearColor
functions.signature: void rlClearColor(unsigned char r, unsigned char g, unsigned char b, unsigned char a);
functions.description: Sets the clear color (glClearColor) from 0-255 channel values.

functions.name: rlClearScreenBuffers
functions.description: Clears color and depth buffers (glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT)).

functions.name: rlCheckErrors
functions.description: Polls and logs GL error codes until no error is left (GL33/ES2). No-op on GL11 path.
requirements: Requires a valid GL context to query errors

functions.name: rlSetBlendMode
functions.description: Sets a predefined blend mode or custom factors previously set. Flushes batch if needed and sets glBlendFunc/Equation.
requirements: mode must be one of rlBlendMode values (e.g., RL_BLEND_ALPHA, RL_BLEND_CUSTOM, RL_BLEND_CUSTOM_SEPARATE)
For custom modes, set factors beforehand via rlSetBlendFactors or rlSetBlendFactorsSeparate

functions.name: rlSetBlendFactors
functions.signature: void rlSetBlendFactors(int glSrcFactor, int glDstFactor, int glEquation);
functions.description: Configures custom blending src/dst factors and equation for RL_BLEND_CUSTOM. Marks state so rlSetBlendMode can apply.
requirements: glSrcFactor, glDstFactor must be valid GL blend factors (e.g., RL_SRC_ALPHA, RL_ONE)
glEquation must be a valid GL blend equation (e.g., RL_FUNC_ADD)

functions.name: rlSetBlendFactorsSeparate
functions.signature: void rlSetBlendFactorsSeparate(int glSrcRGB, int glDstRGB, int glSrcAlpha, int glDstAlpha, int glEqRGB, int glEqAlpha);
functions.description: Configures separate RGB and alpha blending factors/equations for RL_BLEND_CUSTOM_SEPARATE.
requirements: All parameters must be valid GL blend factors/equations

functions.name: rlglInit
functions.description: Initializes rlgl: loads default texture/shader, creates default render batch, sets default GL state, and stores framebuffer size. Must be called once after creating a valid OpenGL context.
requirements: A valid/current OpenGL context must exist prior to calling
Call exactly once per process or ensure rlglClose() before re-init
width and height should match the framebuffer size

functions.name: rlglClose
functions.description: De-initializes rlgl: unloads default batch, default shader, default texture, and software backend if used; resets ready flag.
requirements: Call after rlglInit() when shutting down the GL context to release resources

functions.name: rlLoadExtensions
functions.description: Loads required GL function pointers and queries supported extensions. The loader must match GLAD-style function signature.
requirements: loader must be a function pointer of type (void *(*)(const char *)) returning GL proc addresses
Must be called with a valid GL context active (especially for GL33/ES2/ES3)

functions.name: rlGetProcAddress
functions.description: Returns a GL procedure address using the stored loader from rlLoadExtensions.
requirements: rlLoadExtensions must have been called to set RLGL.loader
procName must be a valid OpenGL function name string

functions.name: rlGetVersion
functions.description: Returns the compile-time selected rlgl OpenGL backend version as rlGlVersion enum value.

functions.name: rlSetFramebufferWidth
functions.description: Sets rlgl’s tracked framebuffer width.
requirements: GL33/ES2 path only; width should be >= 0

functions.name: rlGetFramebufferWidth
functions.description: Returns rlgl’s tracked framebuffer width.

functions.name: rlSetFramebufferHeight
functions.description: Sets rlgl’s tracked framebuffer height.
requirements: GL33/ES2 path only; height should be >= 0

functions.name: rlGetFramebufferHeight
functions.description: Returns rlgl’s tracked framebuffer height.

functions.name: rlGetTextureIdDefault
functions.description: Returns the default 1x1 white RGBA texture id created by rlglInit.
requirements: rlglInit() must have succeeded

functions.name: rlGetShaderIdDefault
functions.description: Returns the default shader program id created by rlglInit.
requirements: rlglInit() must have succeeded

functions.name: rlGetShaderLocsDefault
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the array of default shader uniform/attribute locations.
requirements: Pointer remains valid until rlglClose()

functions.name: rlLoadRenderBatch
functions.description: Creates and initializes a render batch (CPU arrays, GPU VBOs/VAOs, draw call array) for immediate-mode batching.
requirements: rlglInit() must have been called and GPU ready; otherwise returns an empty batch
numBuffers >= 1
bufferElements > 0 indicates quad capacity per buffer

functions.name: rlUnloadRenderBatch
functions.description: Deletes GPU buffers/VAOs associated with the batch and frees CPU-side arrays.
requirements: Batch must have been created by rlLoadRenderBatch

functions.name: rlDrawRenderBatch
functions.description: Uploads current CPU-side vertex data to GPU, sets shader uniforms, binds textures, and issues draw calls for the batch. Resets batch state and advances to next buffer.
requirements: batch must be non-NULL and initialized
Requires current shader/texture state in RLGL.State
If stereo rendering is enabled, sets per-eye viewport and matrices

functions.name: rlSetRenderBatchActive
functions.description: Flushes current batch and sets a new active batch; if NULL, uses the internal default batch.
requirements: batch may be NULL to restore default
Active batch must remain valid during rendering

functions.name: rlDrawRenderBatchActive
functions.description: Flushes and draws the currently active internal batch.
requirements: An active batch must exist (rlglInit creates one)

functions.name: rlCheckRenderBatchLimit
functions.description: Checks if adding vCount vertices would overflow the current batch buffer. If so, flushes the batch and restores draw state. Returns true if an overflow occurred.
requirements: vCount must be >= 0

functions.name: rlSetTexture
functions.description: Sets the current texture for batching; may trigger a batch split to maintain index alignment. Passing 0 unsets and uses default texture.
requirements: id is a valid 2D texture or 0
May force a batch flush if vertex buffer is at capacity or texture changes mid-draw

functions.name: rlLoadVertexArray
functions.description: Generates a vertex array object (VAO) if supported and returns its id, otherwise 0.
requirements: rlglInit and extensions must indicate VAO support

functions.name: rlLoadVertexBuffer
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadVertexBuffer(const void *buffer, int size, bool dynamic);
functions.description: Creates a GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, uploads data of size bytes, using GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW if dynamic is true else GL_STATIC_DRAW. Returns buffer id.
requirements: size must be > 0
buffer may be NULL to allocate without initial data

functions.name: rlLoadVertexBufferElement
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadVertexBufferElement(const void *buffer, int size, bool dynamic);
functions.description: Creates a GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER, uploads data. Returns buffer id.
requirements: size must be > 0
buffer may be NULL

functions.name: rlUpdateVertexBuffer
functions.signature: void rlUpdateVertexBuffer(unsigned int bufferId, const void *data, int dataSize, int offset);
functions.description: Updates a region of an array buffer with new data via glBufferSubData.
requirements: bufferId must be a valid GL_ARRAY_BUFFER
dataSize >= 0, offset >= 0
data must point to at least dataSize bytes

functions.name: rlUpdateVertexBufferElements
functions.signature: void rlUpdateVertexBufferElements(unsigned int id, const void *data, int dataSize, int offset);
functions.description: Updates a region of an element array buffer via glBufferSubData.
requirements: id must be a valid GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER
dataSize >= 0, offset >= 0

functions.name: rlUnloadVertexArray
functions.description: Deletes a VAO by id (if supported) after unbinding.
requirements: vaoId must be a valid VAO name

functions.name: rlUnloadVertexBuffer
functions.description: Deletes a buffer object by id.
requirements: vboId must be a valid GL buffer name

functions.name: rlSetVertexAttribute
functions.signature: void rlSetVertexAttribute(unsigned int index, int compSize, int type, bool normalized, int stride, int offset);
functions.description: Defines an array of generic vertex attribute data at index via glVertexAttribPointer using currently bound array buffer.
requirements: index must be a valid attribute index
compSize in [1..4] per attribute type
type must be a valid GL type for vertex attributes
stride and offset are in bytes; offset is cast to pointer

functions.name: rlSetVertexAttributeDivisor
functions.signature: void rlSetVertexAttributeDivisor(unsigned int index, int divisor);
functions.description: Sets the frequency divisor for instanced rendering for a vertex attribute index.
requirements: Instancing support must be available
index must refer to a valid attribute

functions.name: rlSetVertexAttributeDefault
functions.signature: void rlSetVertexAttributeDefault(int locIndex, const void *value, int attribType, int count);
functions.description: Sets a constant default value for a vertex attribute (not sourced from a buffer).
requirements: attribType must be one of RL_SHADER_ATTRIB_FLOAT, RL_SHADER_ATTRIB_VEC2, RL_SHADER_ATTRIB_VEC3, RL_SHADER_ATTRIB_VEC4
count must match the attribType component count
value must point to enough floats

functions.name: rlDrawVertexArray
functions.description: Issues a glDrawArrays with mode GL_TRIANGLES starting at offset for count vertices.
requirements: Appropriate vertex arrays/attributes must be bound and enabled
offset >= 0, count >= 0

functions.name: rlDrawVertexArrayElements
functions.signature: void rlDrawVertexArrayElements(int offset, int count, const void *buffer);
functions.description: Issues a glDrawElements with GL_TRIANGLES using a client-side or mapped index buffer pointer adjusted by offset (interpreted as GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT).
requirements: buffer must point to at least count indices of GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT
offset is in indices, not bytes; internally converted to pointer offset
count >= 0

functions.name: rlDrawVertexArrayInstanced
functions.signature: void rlDrawVertexArrayInstanced(int offset, int count, int instances);
functions.description: Issues a glDrawArraysInstanced with GL_TRIANGLES for instanced rendering.
requirements: Instancing must be supported
offset >= 0, count >= 0, instances >= 1

functions.name: rlDrawVertexArrayElementsInstanced
functions.signature: void rlDrawVertexArrayElementsInstanced(int offset, int count, const void *buffer, int instances);
functions.description: Issues a glDrawElementsInstanced with GL_TRIANGLES using GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT indices.
requirements: Instancing must be supported
buffer must point to at least count indices
offset is in indices

functions.name: rlLoadTexture
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadTexture(const void *data, int width, int height, int format, int mipmapCount);
functions.description: Creates a 2D texture from raw pixel data and uploads all mip levels. Sets default wrap and filter. Returns GL texture id or 0 on failure.
requirements: A current GL context and GPU readiness are required (rlglInit)
width > 0, height > 0
format must be a supported rlPixelFormat; compressed formats require extension support
data may be NULL to create empty levels; size expectations follow format and mipmapCount
mipmapCount >= 1

functions.name: rlLoadTextureDepth
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadTextureDepth(int width, int height, bool useRenderBuffer);
functions.description: Creates a depth texture or renderbuffer for FBO attachment depending on support and useRenderBuffer flag. Returns id.
requirements: GL depth texture support required for texture path; otherwise a renderbuffer is created
width > 0, height > 0

functions.name: rlLoadTextureCubemap
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadTextureCubemap(const void *data, int size, int format, int mipmapCount);
functions.description: Creates a cubemap texture, uploading 6 faces for each mip level in +X,-X,+Y,-Y,+Z,-Z order. Returns texture id.
requirements: size > 0, mipmapCount >= 1
data may be NULL to allocate empty faces (uncompressed formats only)
format must be supported; compressed formats require support

functions.name: rlUpdateTexture
functions.signature: void rlUpdateTexture(unsigned int id, int offsetX, int offsetY, int width, int height, int format, const void *data);
functions.description: Updates a sub-region of an existing 2D texture with new pixel data using glTexSubImage2D.
requirements: id must be a valid 2D texture
format must be uncompressed; compressed sub-update is not supported by this wrapper
width,height >= 0; offsets within texture bounds
data must point to sufficient pixel data

functions.name: rlGetGlTextureFormats
functions.signature: void rlGetGlTextureFormats(int format, unsigned int *glInternalFormat, unsigned int *glFormat, unsigned int *glType);
functions.description: Translates a rlPixelFormat into corresponding OpenGL internal format, data format, and data type values. Sets 0 when unsupported.
requirements: glInternalFormat, glFormat, glType must be non-NULL pointers
format must be one of rlPixelFormat values

functions.name: rlGetPixelFormatName
functions.description: Returns a string name for the given rlPixelFormat enum value or "UNKNOWN" if unrecognized.

functions.name: rlUnloadTexture
functions.description: Deletes a GL texture by id.
requirements: id must be a valid texture name or 0; deleting 0 is ignored by GL

functions.name: rlGenTextureMipmaps
functions.signature: void rlGenTextureMipmaps(unsigned int id, int width, int height, int format, int *mipmaps);
functions.description: Generates mipmaps for the bound 2D texture via glGenerateMipmap if POT or NPOT supported, and returns total mip count.
requirements: id must be a valid 2D texture
mipmaps must be a non-NULL pointer to receive count
width,height > 0
On ES2 without NPOT support, only POT textures will generate mipmaps

functions.name: rlReadTexturePixels
functions.signature: void *rlReadTexturePixels(unsigned int id, int width, int height, int format);
functions.description: Reads back texture pixels into a newly allocated buffer and returns it. Uses glGetTexImage on GL11/33; on ES2 uses FBO readback. Caller must free the returned memory.
requirements: id must be a valid 2D texture
width,height,format must match the texture contents expected for correct readback
On ES2 path, format is read back as RGBA via FBO regardless of original

functions.name: rlReadScreenPixels
functions.description: Reads RGBA pixels from the current framebuffer using glReadPixels, flips the image vertically, and sets alpha to 255. Returns newly allocated buffer; caller must free.
requirements: width,height > 0
Must be called with a valid GL context and framebuffer size at least width x height

functions.name: rlLoadFramebuffer
functions.description: Generates a framebuffer object and returns its id. Does not attach any textures or renderbuffers.
requirements: Requires a valid GL context

functions.name: rlFramebufferAttach
functions.signature: void rlFramebufferAttach(unsigned int fboId, unsigned int texId, int attachType, int texType, int mipLevel);
functions.description: Attaches a texture/renderbuffer to an FBO at the specified attachment point (color channel, depth, or stencil).
requirements: fboId must refer to a valid FBO
attachType must be one of RL_ATTACHMENT_*
texType must be RL_ATTACHMENT_TEXTURE2D, RL_ATTACHMENT_RENDERBUFFER, or a cubemap face constant
texId must be a valid texture/renderbuffer name for the given type
mipLevel >= 0

functions.name: rlFramebufferComplete
functions.description: Binds an FBO and checks its completeness via glCheckFramebufferStatus, logging issues, returns true if complete.
requirements: id must be a valid FBO name

functions.name: rlUnloadFramebuffer
functions.description: Deletes an FBO and also deletes any attached depth texture/renderbuffer (queried) before deleting the FBO.
requirements: id must be a valid FBO name or 0 (0 is ignored)

functions.name: rlCopyFramebuffer
functions.signature: void rlCopyFramebuffer(int x, int y, int width, int height, int format, void *pixels);
functions.description: Software-backend-only helper that copies framebuffer pixels into a user buffer via the software renderer.
requirements: Only valid for GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_11_SOFTWARE backend
pixels must point to enough memory for the requested rectangle in the translated GL format

functions.name: rlResizeFramebuffer
functions.description: Software-backend-only: resizes the internal software framebuffer.
requirements: Only valid for GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_11_SOFTWARE backend
width,height > 0

functions.name: rlLoadShaderCode
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadShaderCode(const char *vsCode, const char *fsCode);
functions.description: Compiles provided vertex/fragment shader source (or uses defaults if NULL) and links a shader program. Returns program id, falling back to default program on failure.
requirements: A valid GL context required
vsCode/fsCode must be null-terminated GLSL source strings or NULL
On success may reuse default shader ids without relinking

functions.name: rlCompileShader
functions.signature: unsigned int rlCompileShader(const char *shaderCode, int type);
functions.description: Compiles a single shader object of given type (GL_VERTEX_SHADER, GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, GL_COMPUTE_SHADER on GL43). Returns shader id or 0 on compile error and logs info log.
requirements: shaderCode must be a null-terminated GLSL source string
type must be a supported GL shader enum for the active backend

functions.name: rlLoadShaderProgram
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadShaderProgram(unsigned int vShaderId, unsigned int fShaderId);
functions.description: Links a program from provided compiled vertex and fragment shader objects, binds default attribute locations, and returns the program id or 0 on failure.
requirements: vShaderId and fShaderId must be valid compiled shader object names
A valid GL context required

functions.name: rlUnloadShaderProgram
functions.description: Deletes a shader program object.
requirements: id must be a valid GL program name or 0

functions.name: rlGetLocationUniform
functions.signature: int rlGetLocationUniform(unsigned int shaderId, const char *uniformName);
functions.description: Returns the location of a uniform in a program using glGetUniformLocation or -1 if not found.
requirements: shaderId must be a valid linked program
uniformName must be a null-terminated string

functions.name: rlGetLocationAttrib
functions.signature: int rlGetLocationAttrib(unsigned int shaderId, const char *attribName);
functions.description: Returns the location of an attribute in a program using glGetAttribLocation or -1 if not found.
requirements: shaderId must be a valid linked program
attribName must be a null-terminated string

functions.name: rlSetUniform
functions.signature: void rlSetUniform(int locIndex, const void *value, int uniformType, int count);
functions.description: Sets shader uniform(s) at locIndex based on type (float/int/uint vectors or sampler index).
requirements: locIndex must be a valid uniform location
uniformType must be a rlShaderUniformDataType value
value must point to at least count elements of the appropriate base type
count >= 1

functions.name: rlSetUniformMatrix
functions.description: Uploads a 4x4 matrix uniform at locIndex (no transpose).
requirements: locIndex must be a valid uniform location

functions.name: rlSetUniformMatrices
functions.signature: void rlSetUniformMatrices(int locIndex, const Matrix *mat, int count);
functions.description: Uploads an array of 4x4 matrices to a uniform array. Uses transpose=true on GL33, false on ES2 per platform needs.
requirements: locIndex must be a valid uniform location
mat must point to at least count matrices
count >= 1

functions.name: rlSetUniformSampler
functions.signature: void rlSetUniformSampler(int locIndex, unsigned int textureId);
functions.description: Assigns a sampler uniform to an available texture unit for batching. Tracks active texture ids and sets the uniform to unit index.
requirements: locIndex must be a valid uniform location for sampler2D
textureId must be a valid texture name
Only up to RL_DEFAULT_BATCH_MAX_TEXTURE_UNITS additional textures tracked (default 4)

functions.name: rlSetShader
functions.description: Switches the currently active shader for batching; flushes current batch if changing. Also updates the current locations pointer.
requirements: id must be a valid GL program
locs must point to an array of RL_MAX_SHADER_LOCATIONS ints valid for the program

functions.name: rlLoadComputeShaderProgram
functions.description: Links a compute shader program from a compiled compute shader object (GL43). Returns program id or 0 on failure.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
shaderId must be a compiled GL_COMPUTE_SHADER object

functions.name: rlComputeShaderDispatch
functions.signature: void rlComputeShaderDispatch(unsigned int groupX, unsigned int groupY, unsigned int groupZ);
functions.description: Dispatches a compute shader with the specified work group counts (GL43).
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
groupX, groupY, groupZ >= 1 as appropriate to your shader

functions.name: rlLoadShaderBuffer
functions.signature: unsigned int rlLoadShaderBuffer(unsigned int size, const void *data, int usageHint);
functions.description: Creates a Shader Storage Buffer Object (SSBO), initializes it with optional data, and returns its id. Optionally clears to zero if data is NULL.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
size > 0
usageHint should be a valid GL buffer usage (e.g., RL_STREAM_COPY, GL_DYNAMIC_DRAW)

functions.name: rlUnloadShaderBuffer
functions.description: Deletes an SSBO by id.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
ssboId must be a valid buffer name

functions.name: rlUpdateShaderBuffer
functions.signature: void rlUpdateShaderBuffer(unsigned int id, const void *data, unsigned int dataSize, unsigned int offset);
functions.description: Updates a subrange of an SSBO with new data via glBufferSubData.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
id must be a valid GL_SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER object
dataSize >= 0, offset >= 0

functions.name: rlBindShaderBuffer
functions.signature: void rlBindShaderBuffer(unsigned int id, unsigned int index);
functions.description: Binds an SSBO to a binding point index via glBindBufferBase.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
id must be a valid SSBO
index must match the binding in the compute/graphics shader

functions.name: rlReadShaderBuffer
functions.signature: void rlReadShaderBuffer(unsigned int id, void *dest, unsigned int count, unsigned int offset);
functions.description: Reads back data from an SSBO into CPU memory via glGetBufferSubData.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
id must be a valid SSBO
dest must point to at least count bytes
offset,count in bytes

functions.name: rlCopyShaderBuffer
functions.signature: void rlCopyShaderBuffer(unsigned int destId, unsigned int srcId, unsigned int destOffset, unsigned int srcOffset, unsigned int count);
functions.description: Copies a subrange of data between two buffers using glCopyBufferSubData.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
destId and srcId must be valid buffer names
Offsets and count are in bytes; regions must be within bounds

functions.name: rlGetShaderBufferSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the given SSBO using glGetBufferParameteri64v, or 0 if unsupported.
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
id must be a valid SSBO boundable object

functions.name: rlBindImageTexture
functions.signature: void rlBindImageTexture(unsigned int id, unsigned int index, int format, bool readonly);
functions.description: Binds a texture as an image for load/store in shaders at the given unit index with access mode (read-only or read-write).
requirements: Requires GRAPHICS_API_OPENGL_43
id must be a valid texture name
index is the image unit
format must be a supported rlPixelFormat that maps to a valid GL internal format

functions.name: rlGetMatrixModelview
functions.description: Returns the current modelview matrix (queried from GL on GL11, or from rlgl state on GL33/ES2).

functions.name: rlGetMatrixProjection
functions.description: Returns the current projection matrix (queried from GL on GL11, or from rlgl state on GL33/ES2).

functions.name: rlGetMatrixTransform
functions.description: Returns the current accumulated transform matrix used for immediate-mode transforms (GL33/ES2 path).

functions.name: rlGetMatrixProjectionStereo
functions.description: Returns the projection matrix for the specified stereo eye (0=right, 1=left in this implementation’s storage order).
requirements: Valid only when stereo matrices have been set; eye must be 0 or 1

functions.name: rlGetMatrixViewOffsetStereo
functions.description: Returns the view offset matrix for the specified stereo eye.
requirements: eye must be 0 or 1

functions.name: rlSetMatrixProjection
functions.description: Sets the internal projection matrix, replacing the current one.

functions.name: rlSetMatrixModelview
functions.description: Sets the internal modelview matrix, replacing the current one.

functions.name: rlSetMatrixProjectionStereo
functions.description: Sets the stereo projection matrices for right and left eyes.

functions.name: rlSetMatrixViewOffsetStereo
functions.description: Sets the stereo view offset matrices for right and left eyes.

functions.name: rlLoadDrawCube
functions.description: Convenience function that creates a temporary VAO/VBO for a unit cube in NDC, draws it, and deletes the buffers.
requirements: Requires GL33/ES2 backend
Must be called with a valid shader bound expecting position/normal/texcoord attributes at default locations

functions.name: rlLoadDrawQuad
functions.description: Convenience function that creates a temporary VAO/VBO for a full-screen quad in NDC, draws it as triangle strip, and deletes the buffers.
requirements: Requires GL33/ES2 backend
Must be called with a valid shader bound expecting position/texcoord attributes at default locations

functions.name: Lerp

functions.description: Linear interpolation between start and end by amount in [0,1] (not enforced).

functions.description: Normalize value into the 0..1 range given an input range [start, end].

functions.name: Remap

functions.description: Map a value from input range to output range using linear mapping.
requirements: inputEnd - inputStart must not be 0 to avoid division by zero.

functions.name: Wrap
functions.signature: RMAPI float Wrap(float value, float min, float max)
functions.description: Wrap a value to the interval [min, max), repeating with period (max - min).
requirements: max - min must not be 0 to avoid division by zero.

functions.name: FloatEquals
functions.signature: RMAPI int FloatEquals(float x, float y)
functions.description: Approximate float equality comparison using an EPSILON-scaled tolerance.

functions.description: Create a Vector2 with all components 0.

functions.description: Create a Vector2 with all components 1.

functions.description: Component-wise addition of two Vector2 values.

functions.description: Add a scalar to both components of a Vector2.

functions.name: Vector2Subtract
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Subtract(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Component-wise subtraction v1 - v2 for Vector2.

functions.name: Vector2SubtractValue
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2SubtractValue(Vector2 v, float sub)
functions.description: Subtract a scalar from both components of a Vector2.

functions.name: Vector2Length
functions.description: Euclidean length (magnitude) of a Vector2.

functions.name: Vector2LengthSqr
functions.description: Squared length of a Vector2 (avoids sqrt).

functions.name: Vector2DotProduct

functions.description: Dot product of two Vector2 values.

functions.name: Vector2CrossProduct
functions.signature: RMAPI float Vector2CrossProduct(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: 2D scalar cross product (v1.x*v2.y - v1.y*v2.x).

functions.name: Vector2Distance
functions.signature: RMAPI float Vector2Distance(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Euclidean distance between two Vector2 points.

functions.name: Vector2DistanceSqr
functions.signature: RMAPI float Vector2DistanceSqr(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Squared distance between two Vector2 points.

functions.name: Vector2Angle
functions.signature: RMAPI float Vector2Angle(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Signed angle from v1 to v2 using atan2(det, dot). Coordinates assume +X right, +Y down.

functions.name: Vector2LineAngle
functions.signature: RMAPI float Vector2LineAngle(Vector2 start, Vector2 end)
functions.description: Angle of the line from start to end, clockwise-positive per implementation note.
requirements: start and end must be normalized vectors per comment (Parameters need to be normalized).

functions.name: Vector2Scale
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Scale(Vector2 v, float scale)
functions.description: Scale a Vector2 by a scalar.

functions.name: Vector2Multiply
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Multiply(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Component-wise multiplication of two Vector2 values.

functions.name: Vector2Negate
functions.description: Negate both components of a Vector2.

functions.name: Vector2Divide
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Divide(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Component-wise division v1 / v2 for Vector2.
requirements: v2.x and v2.y must not be 0 to avoid division by zero.

functions.name: Vector2Normalize
functions.description: Return the normalized (unit-length) Vector2; returns zero vector if input has zero length.

functions.name: Vector2Transform
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Transform(Vector2 v, Matrix mat)
functions.description: Transform a 2D vector by a 4x4 matrix (assumes z=0, w=1).

functions.name: Vector2Lerp
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Lerp(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2, float amount)
functions.description: Linear interpolation between two Vector2 values.

functions.name: Vector2Reflect
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Reflect(Vector2 v, Vector2 normal)
functions.description: Reflect incident vector v about a plane with given normal.

functions.name: Vector2Min
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Min(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Component-wise minimum of two Vector2 values.

functions.name: Vector2Max
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Max(Vector2 v1, Vector2 v2)
functions.description: Component-wise maximum of two Vector2 values.

functions.name: Vector2Rotate
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Rotate(Vector2 v, float angle)
functions.description: Rotate a Vector2 by angle (radians).
requirements: angle is in radians.

functions.name: Vector2MoveTowards
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2MoveTowards(Vector2 v, Vector2 target, float maxDistance)
functions.description: Move point v towards target by up to maxDistance; clamps when within range.

functions.name: Vector2Invert
functions.description: Component-wise inversion (1/x) of Vector2.
requirements: v.x and v.y must not be 0 to avoid division by zero.

functions.name: Vector2Clamp
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Clamp(Vector2 v, Vector2 min, Vector2 max)
functions.description: Clamp Vector2 components between corresponding min and max components.

functions.name: Vector2ClampValue
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2ClampValue(Vector2 v, float min, float max)
functions.description: Clamp the magnitude of v between min and max, preserving direction.
requirements: min and max should be non-negative magnitudes for meaningful results (inferred from usage).

functions.name: Vector2Equals
functions.signature: RMAPI int Vector2Equals(Vector2 p, Vector2 q)
functions.description: Approximate equality of two Vector2 values using component-wise EPSILON-based tolerance.

functions.name: Vector2Refract
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector2 Vector2Refract(Vector2 v, Vector2 n, float r)
functions.description: Compute refraction direction given incident v, surface normal n, and index ratio r. Returns zero vector if total internal reflection.
requirements: v and n should be normalized for correct optics.

functions.description: Create a Vector3 with all components 0.

functions.description: Create a Vector3 with all components 1.

functions.signature: RMAPI Vector3 Vector3Add(Vector3 v1, Vector3 v2)
functions.description: Component-wise addition of two Vector3 values.

functions.name: Vector3AddValue
functions.signature: RMAPI Vector3 Vector3AddValue(Vector3 v, float add)
functions.description: Add a scalar to all components of a Vector3.

functions.signature: RMAPI Vector3 Vector3Subtract(Vector3 v1, Vector3 v2)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets APIs that consume UTF-8 C-strings via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and
# filenames via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME. We produce a single bytes buffer that embeds
# multiple null-terminated UTF-8 strings and plausible file paths so the fuzzer
# can slice/consume them in sequence.
#
# Coverage goals per stub:
# - InitWindow/SetWindowTitle: short, long, unicode, control chars, format-like strings
# - SetClipboardText: arbitrary text including newlines and emojis
# - TraceLog: provide strings that might include percent signs and numbers
# - SaveFileText: filename-like path + .txt, content with various line endings
# - FileTextReplace/FileTextFindIndex: filename plus search/replacement tokens
# - IsFileExtension: realistic filename with typical extensions
# - MakeDirectory: directory path patterns
# - IsFileNameValid: include invalid characters on some platforms
# - SetGamepadMappings: SDL-style mapping line samples
#
# Buffer format:
# A concatenation of null-terminated UTF-8 strings and paths in a mixed order.
# The fuzzer framework will typically read sequential bytes to fulfill FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# or FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME requests. All strings are valid UTF-8 and NUL-terminated.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,+()[]{}#@!$%&=~^"  # exclude '/' for filenames body, add later as separators

EMOJIS = [
    "😀", "😂", "🥺", "👍", "🔥", "✨", "🎮", "🖱️", "⌨️", "🧪", "🧰", "📁", "📄", "📝", "🧵"
]

UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    (0x00A1, 0x00FF),   # Latin-1 Supplement
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
    (0x3040, 0x309F),   # Hiragana
    (0x30A0, 0x30FF),   # Katakana
    (0x4E00, 0x4E80),   # a subset of CJK Unified Ideographs (keep range small)
]

COMMON_EXTS = [
    "txt", "md", "log", "cfg", "ini", "json", "xml", "csv", "html", "bin", "dat"
]

# Forbidden characters in filenames on Windows (we still include them for IsFileNameValid coverage)
INVALID_FN_CHARS = "<>:\\\\|?*\""  # note: backslash escaped


def rand_unicode(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII, emojis, and random codepoints from selected blocks
    parts: List[str] = []
    # ASCII run
    parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 16))))
    # Emoji sprinkle
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        parts.append(rng.choice(EMOJIS))
    # Random codepoints from blocks
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 4)):
        lo, hi = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
        cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        parts.append(chr(cp))
    # Optional newlines/tabs
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append("\n")
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append("\r\n")
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append("\t")
    return ''.join(parts)


def rand_title(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    variants = [
        "Raylib Fuzz",
        "Window 🚪 ",
        "%s %d title",  # include printf-like
        rand_unicode(rng),
    ]
    s = rng.choice(variants)
    # Length diversify
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        s += " - " + ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII_SAFE) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 32)))
    return s


def rand_filename_component(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12, allow_invalid=False) -> str:
    base_chars = ASCII_SAFE.replace('/', '')
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(base_chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(min_len, max_len)))
    # Optionally inject unicode in component
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        s += rng.choice(EMOJIS)
    # Optionally inject invalid chars to test IsFileNameValid
    if allow_invalid and rng.random() < 0.5:
        s = s[:-1] + rng.choice(INVALID_FN_CHARS)
    return s or "a"


def rand_path(rng: random.Random, as_file=True, allow_invalid=False) -> str:
    # Generate Unix-like or Windows-like path
    parts: List[str] = []
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        # Windows drive
        drive = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters).upper() + ":\\"  # backslashes
        parts.append(drive)
        sep = "\\"
    else:
        sep = "/"
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append("/")
    depth = rng.randint(1, 4)
    comps = [rand_filename_component(rng, allow_invalid=allow_invalid) for _ in range(depth)]
    path = ('' if parts and parts[0] == "/" else '').join(parts) + sep.join(c.strip() for c in comps)
    if as_file:
        ext = rng.choice(COMMON_EXTS)
        path = path + "." + ext
    return path


def rand_gamepad_mapping(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Very rough SDL_GameControllerDB-like mapping
    # format: guid,name,a:b1,b:b2,...
    guid = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(32))
    name = "FuzzPad" + str(rng.randint(1, 99))
    pairs = [
        "a:b0", "b:b1", "x:b2", "y:b3",
        "back:b4", "guide:b5", "start:b6",
        "leftstick:b7", "rightstick:b8",
        "leftshoulder:b9", "rightshoulder:b10",
        "dpup:h0.1", "dpleft:h0.8", "dpdown:h0.4", "dpright:h0.2",
        "leftx:a0", "lefty:a1", "rightx:a2", "righty:a3",
        "lefttrigger:a4", "righttrigger:a5",
    ]
    rng.shuffle(pairs)
    return f"{guid},{name},{','.join(pairs)}"


def cstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'strict') + b"\x00"


def bounded_concat(chunks: List[bytes], limit: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for ch in chunks:
        if len(out) + len(ch) > limit:
            break
        out.extend(ch)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Titles for InitWindow/SetWindowTitle
    for _ in range(3):
        chunks.append(cstr(rand_title(rng)))

    # Clipboard texts (include varied newlines and unicode)
    for _ in range(2):
        s = rand_unicode(rng)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s += "\r\nEnd"
        chunks.append(cstr(s))

    # TraceLog strings with percent and numeric patterns
    trace_variants = [
        "Log: %s %d",
        "value=%d name=%s",
        "normal text",
        rand_unicode(rng)
    ]
    for s in trace_variants:
        chunks.append(cstr(s))

    # SaveFileText: plausible paths and contents
    for _ in range(2):
        path = rand_path(rng, as_file=True, allow_invalid=False)
        chunks.append(cstr(path))
        content = rand_unicode(rng)
        # Ensure within typical size cap used by stub (<=1024) but we can be shorter
        if len(content.encode('utf-8')) > 900:
            content = content[:300]
        chunks.append(cstr(content))

    # FileTextReplace/FileTextFindIndex: filenames and search/repl tokens
    for _ in range(3):
        chunks.append(cstr(rand_path(rng, as_file=True, allow_invalid=False)))
        chunks.append(cstr(rand_unicode(rng)))  # search
        chunks.append(cstr(rand_unicode(rng)))  # replacement

    # IsFileExtension: file and varied extension strings including with dot
    for ext in [".txt", ".md", ".json", ".png", ".data", ".r\n"]:
        chunks.append(cstr(rand_path(rng, as_file=True, allow_invalid=False)))
        chunks.append(cstr(ext))

    # MakeDirectory: directory paths
    for _ in range(2):
        base = rand_path(rng, as_file=False, allow_invalid=False)
        # Ensure ends like a directory
        if not base.endswith('/') and not base.endswith('\\'):
            base += ("/" if "/" in base or not (":" in base) else "\\")
        dirpath = base + "fuzz_dir"
        chunks.append(cstr(dirpath))

    # IsFileNameValid: include valid and invalid names
    valid_names = [
        "readme.txt", "data.json", "notes.md", "config.ini",
        rand_filename_component(rng) + ".log"
    ]
    invalid_names = [
        "con", "nul", "aux",  # reserved on Windows
        "bad" + rng.choice(list(INVALID_FN_CHARS)),
        "pipe|name.txt",
        "star*name.txt",
        "quest?name.txt",
        "quote\"name.txt",
        "angle<name>.txt"
    ]
    for s in valid_names + invalid_names:
        chunks.append(cstr(s))

    # SetGamepadMappings sample lines
    for _ in range(2):
        chunks.append(cstr(rand_gamepad_mapping(rng)))

    # Additional generic UTF-8 strings to satisfy extra FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers
    for _ in range(4):
        chunks.append(cstr(rand_unicode(rng)))

    # Ensure total size <= MAX_TOTAL
    buf = bounded_concat(chunks, MAX_TOTAL)
    return buf

import random
from typing import List

def _rand_ident(r: random.Random, prefix: str = "v") -> str:
    letters = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    return prefix + "_" + "".join(r.choice(letters) for _ in range(r.randint(4, 10)))

def _gen_vertex_shader(r: random.Random, version: int) -> str:
    # Generate minimal but valid vertex shader with some variability
    use_inout = version >= 330
    lines: List[str] = []
    lines.append(f"#version {version}")
    # precision qualifiers are ignored in desktop, but allowed; keep fragment-only usually
    # Attributes
    a_pos = _rand_ident(r, "aPos")
    a_col = _rand_ident(r, "aCol")
    a_tex = _rand_ident(r, "aTex")
    if use_inout:
        lines.append(f"layout(location=0) in vec3 {a_pos};")
        lines.append(f"layout(location=1) in vec2 {a_tex};")
        lines.append(f"layout(location=2) in vec4 {a_col};")
        vcol = _rand_ident(r, "vCol")
        vtex = _rand_ident(r, "vTex")
        lines.append(f"out vec4 {vcol};")
        lines.append(f"out vec2 {vtex};")
    else:
        lines.append(f"attribute vec3 {a_pos};")
        lines.append(f"attribute vec2 {a_tex};")
        lines.append(f"attribute vec4 {a_col};")
        vcol = _rand_ident(r, "vCol")
        vtex = _rand_ident(r, "vTex")
        lines.append(f"varying vec4 {vcol};")
        lines.append(f"varying vec2 {vtex};")

    # Uniforms typical for raylib
    mvp = _rand_ident(r, "uMVP")
    lines.append(f"uniform mat4 {mvp};")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        timeu = _rand_ident(r, "uTime")
        lines.append(f"uniform float {timeu};")
    else:
        timeu = None

    lines.append("void main() {")
    lines.append(f"    {vcol} = {a_col};")
    if timeu:
        lines.append(f"    {vtex} = {a_tex} + vec2(sin({timeu})*0.0, 0.0);")
    else:
        lines.append(f"    {vtex} = {a_tex};")
    # Optional minor math variation
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        lines.append(f"    gl_Position = {mvp} * vec4({a_pos}, 1.0);")
    else:
        lines.append(f"    vec4 p = vec4({a_pos}.xy, {a_pos}.z, 1.0);")
        lines.append(f"    gl_Position = {mvp} * p;")
    lines.append("}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def _gen_fragment_shader(r: random.Random, version: int) -> str:
    use_inout = version >= 330
    lines: List[str] = []
    lines.append(f"#version {version}")

    # precision qualifiers help on ES; harmless on desktop if ignored
    if version in (100, 300):
        lines.append("precision mediump float;")

    vcol = _rand_ident(r, "vCol")
    vtex = _rand_ident(r, "vTex")
    if use_inout:
        lines.append(f"in vec4 {vcol};")
        lines.append(f"in vec2 {vtex};")
        frag = _rand_ident(r, "fragColor")
        lines.append(f"out vec4 {frag};")
    else:
        lines.append(f"varying vec4 {vcol};")
        lines.append(f"varying vec2 {vtex};")
        frag = None  # use gl_FragColor

    # Sampler optional
    sam = _rand_ident(r, "tex0") if r.random() < 0.8 else None
    if sam:
        lines.append(f"uniform sampler2D {sam};")

    # Extra uniforms
    tint = _rand_ident(r, "uTint") if r.random() < 0.7 else None
    if tint:
        lines.append(f"uniform vec4 {tint};")

    lines.append("void main() {")
    if sam:
        lines.append(f"    vec4 col = texture({sam}, {vtex});")
    else:
        lines.append(f"    vec4 col = {vcol};")
    if tint:
        lines.append(f"    col *= {tint};")

    if frag:
        lines.append(f"    {frag} = col;")
    else:
        lines.append("    gl_FragColor = col;")
    lines.append("}")

    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def _choose_version(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Prefer commonly supported desktop GLSL versions and include some ES variants
    versions = [330, 100, 120, 300, 150]
    weights = [0.45, 0.1, 0.15, 0.15, 0.15]
    return r.choices(versions, weights=weights, k=1)[0]

def _package_as_dual_file_blob(vs_src: str, fs_src: str, r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # The fuzzer stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME twice, each gets a file with fuzz data.
    # Some fuzzers concatenate multiple logical files in one buffer separated by a marker.
    # We provide a simple container format:
    # b"VS\0" + u32le vs_len + vs + b"FS\0" + u32le fs_len + fs
    import struct
    vs_b = vs_src.encode("utf-8")
    fs_b = fs_src.encode("utf-8")
    blob = bytearray()
    blob += b"VS\x00" + struct.pack("<I", len(vs_b)) + vs_b
    blob += b"FS\x00" + struct.pack("<I", len(fs_b)) + fs_b
    # Keep within 4096
    return bytes(blob[:4096])

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    version = _choose_version(r)
    vs = _gen_vertex_shader(r, version)
    fs = _gen_fragment_shader(r, version)

    # Occasionally cross-link uniforms/IO names to increase chance of matching
    # Ensure varying names match between stages
    # Recreate fragment with the exact varying names from vertex
    # Extract last generated varying names by regenerating deterministically with same Random state snapshot
    # Instead, synchronize by regenerating both from a shared plan
    r2 = random.Random(seed + 1)
    version = _choose_version(r2)
    vs = _gen_vertex_shader(r2, version)
    fs = _gen_fragment_shader(r2, version)

    return _package_as_dual_file_blob(vs, fs, r2)

# Data type: identifier string
# Used by stubs as candidate uniform names for GetShaderLocation/SetShaderValue*/
# Goal: produce a bytes blob that the harness will split into FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# We therefore pack multiple null-terminated C strings back-to-back to seed the fuzzer
# with interesting uniform identifiers, including common names and a variety of shapes.

COMMON_UNIFORMS = [
    # Very common matrices and vectors
    "mvp", "MVP", "uMVP", "model", "view", "projection",
    "modelView", "modelViewProjection", "normalMatrix",
    # Colors and tints
    "tint", "uTint", "color", "diffuseColor", "specularColor", "ambientColor",

    # Misc
    "time", "uTime", "resolution", "uResolution", "screenSize", "cameraPos",
]

    "_", "__", "a", "A", "u0", "u1", "x", "y", "z", "w",
    "uVec2", "uVec3", "uVec4", "uInt", "iVec4",
    # Long snake case
    "very_long_uniform_name_for_testing_shader_lookup_paths_0001",
    # Mixed case and digits
    "Uniform123_NAME_mVp_TiNt",
    # With array-like suffixes often used for arrays
    "bones[0]", "bones[1]", "weights[0]", "weights[3]",
    # Dots and namespaces sometimes seen in engines
    "material.albedo", "material.roughness", "camera.view",
    # Unicode identifier-like (UTF-8)
    "μTime", "цвет", "名前",
]

MATRIX_BASES = ["mvp", "model", "view", "projection", "modelView", "modelViewProjection"]
MATRIX_SUFFIXES = ["", "Matrix", "_matrix", "Mat", "_mat", "Mat4", "_mat4"]
COLOR_BASES = ["tint", "color", "diffuse", "specular", "ambient"]
COLOR_SUFFIXES = ["", "Color", "_color", "Col", "_rgba"]

    "texture", "albedo", "metalness", "normal", "roughness", "occlusion",
    "emission", "height", "cubemap", "irradiance", "prefilter", "brdf"
]

def _rand_ident(rng: random.Random, length_range=(3, 24)) -> str:
    letters = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
    n = rng.randint(*length_range)
    # Ensure starts with letter or underscore for typical identifiers
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    rest = "".join(rng.choice(letters) for _ in range(n - 1))

def _build_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
